A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Re3Align, REspGen, and REspEval work. All 26 pages of v1.pdf and 29 pages of v2.pdf, including appendices A–D, support comparison; relocated text and renumbered figures can be matched.

before.justification: v1.pdf reports original generation experiments with five LLMs on 48 instances, alignment-classifier results, and two human evaluation studies.

after.justification: v2.pdf retains those original experiments and human studies and additionally presents individual response-generation case studies.

M1.justification: Alignment, response planning, length control, retrieval, and evaluation-guided refinement remain unchanged. Section 4.2 newly characterizes existing input formats as rough ideas versus contextualized revisions without changing the procedure or prompts.

E1.justification: Both versions retain EMNLP24 and PeerJ coverage, Re3-Sci/ARIES alignment training data, and the 48-instance generation evaluation. The new cases illustrate retained settings rather than introducing a new dataset or task.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains Phi-4, Qwen3, Llama-3.3, DeepSeek, GPT-4o, and human responses. Table 4 also retains the same alignment-classifier comparison set.

E3.justification: The data splits, 48-instance selection, nine experimental settings, prompts, metrics, five-paragraph retrieval, and human-response-length-plus-50 limit are unchanged. The case studies compare existing Settings 2 and 3 without introducing a different protocol.

E4.justification: New Sections 6.3 and D.3 examine two cases where additional paragraph context accompanies lower response quality or input coverage. Existing robustness and refinement analyses remain; discourse analysis moves from D.2.1 to 6.2.5 rather than being newly added.

E5.justification: Three-run consistency checks, standard deviations, ICC, human agreement statistics, and paired t-tests/Wilcoxon tests are retained. The new cases introduce no additional uncertainty-estimation or repeated-run reporting.

E6.justification: New Settings 2-versus-3 results include DeepSeek targeting 4 versus 2, specificity 3 versus 1, and convincingness 3 versus 1 (Figure 15), plus GPT-4o specificity 4 versus 3 and ICR 0.83 versus 0.75 (Figure 16). Existing aggregate table results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The alignment formalization and order-fidelity definition are unchanged. New Figures 4–5 explanations illustrate existing notation; mathematics quoted in the new response case study does not introduce theory for this work.

C1.justification: The dataset, author-in-the-loop generation framework, evaluation suite, and principal findings remain the same. Rewritten abstract and introduction framing emphasizes existing formulation and evaluation gaps without materially changing contribution scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations connecting contextual inputs to distraction, omitted core details, and lower quality or coverage. Sections 4.2 and 5 clarify what input formats simulate and why quality indicates effectiveness. The dedicated Limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: Table 12 newly identifies Genius1237/xlm-roberta-large-tydip as the politeness model, resolving v1's unsupported footnote marker. The code repository pointer changes from arxiv2026-respgen-respeval to acl2026-respgen-respeval. Existing prompts, hardware information, and dataset access remain.

R1.justification: The bibliography and Table 1's prior-work comparison are unchanged. Revised introductory emphasis preserves the existing positioning around author signals, controllability, and evaluation; citations within new example excerpts do not change that positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are reframed around formulation and evaluation questions, and 'input design' becomes 'input specificity.' Discourse discussion moves into the main text and case-study subsections are added, while most prose and the overall section structure remain.

P2.justification: v2 annotates Figure 4, adds an edit-alignment illustration as Figure 5 and case-study Figures 15–16, expands Tables 3 and 12 captions, and reflows appendix figures and tables. Existing result charts and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Clearer framing, alignment illustrations, setting captions, and the explicit politeness-model identifier modestly improve readability and reproducibility. The new cases make individual outcomes inspectable, although Figure 15 favors a response asserting a document choice not established by its displayed input, weakening that interpretation. With the core empirical validation unchanged, the overall gain is limited.
